newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Fischler calls for fairer sharing of EU farm aid.
newsitem.headline: Fischler calls for fairer sharing of EU farm aid.

text.p: Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler on Friday called for farm subsidies to be shared more equally and for limits on payments to large, wealthy farmers.
At present 80 percent of EU farm subsidies are pocketed by 20 percent of the EU's estimated eight million farmers.
"Member states or regions should be allowed to introduce differentiation criteria within commonly agreed limits," Fischler said in a speech for the Centre for European Policy Studies.
However Fischler said that making payments according to farm size could be difficult to to put into practice.
For instance small farmers could be earning substantial revenue from off-farm activities while large farms could provide many jobs.
Proposals for so-called modulation of EU farm aid as part of 1992 farm reforms were rejected after opposition from Britain and other member states.
Fischler also reiterated the need, highlighted in April, for urgent reforms to prevent grain, beef and dairy surpluses reappearing.
"A new crisis of overproduction is looming rather sooner than later," he warned.
